anomalies.observed: Net TX_GPIO14 contains U20.2 (3.3V LDO output, VO), Module1.55 (CM4 GPIO14), and U21.4 (FT231XS RXD), merging the 3.3V power rail with the UART TX/RX signals.
anomalies.expected: The 3.3V regulator output should be a dedicated power net (e.g., +3V3) separate from the UART TX net (Module1.55 and U21.4).
anomalies.impact: The 3.3V rail is shorted to CM4 GPIO14 and FT231XS RXD. This will prevent UART communication, cause the CM4 GPIO to fight the 3.3V regulator, and likely damage components or prevent boot.

anomalies.observed: Net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23, with no connection to any power source.
anomalies.expected: The anodes of these LEDs should be connected to a 3.3V supply rail (e.g., TX_GPIO14 or a switched 3.3V net) so they can illuminate.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet and activity LEDs D4, D14, and D23 will never turn on because their anodes are floating.

anomalies.observed: U13.9 and U14.9 (I2C/SPI mode select pins) are tied to GND, while the devices are wired with SPI signals on pins 10-13 (SERIAL_CIPO, SERIAL_COPI, SERIAL_CLK, CS1/CS2).
anomalies.expected: For SPI operation, U13.9 and U14.9 must be tied high to the 3.3V logic rail (SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V), not to GND.
anomalies.impact: The SC16IS752 UART expanders will be held in I2C mode, so the SPI interface will not work and the serial ports will be nonfunctional.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple serious anomalies: the 3.3V rail is shorted to CM4 GPIO14 and FT231XS RXD, the Ethernet/activity LED anodes are left floating, and the SC16IS752 UART expanders have their SPI mode-select pins tied to ground. These would cause major functional failures.
